newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian president sworn in for second term.
newsitem.headline: Estonian president sworn in for second term.

text.p: Estonian President Lennart Meri was sworn in for a second term of office on Monday, saying he wanted the small Baltic state to be "an everlasting part" of Europe.
Meri was re-elected on September 20, having been forced to go through five gruelling rounds of voting, three in parliament and two in a specially-called electoral college.

He will lead Estonia for the next five years, likely to be a crucial time for the former Soviet republic which is bidding with its two fellow Baltic neighbours for membership of the European Union (EU) and NATO.

Estonia regained its independence from the former Soviet Union in 1991 and has set its sights on both EU and NATO membership although it and fellow Balts Latvia and Lithuania are unlikely to be part of a first wave of NATO enlargement.

"We are heading towards a state where the individual is in the centre, which is open to innovation, self-fulfilment and the retention of Estonian culture as an everlasting part of European culture," Meri told parliament after his swearing-in.
Meri, although well-respected on the international stage, had to fight hard to be re-elected as parliamentarians accused him of abusing his largely ceremonial position.
He failed three times to get parliament's support for re-election and the vote went to a special electoral college, which chose him for another term in the second and final vote.

The main accusation against him was that he signed an agreement in 1994 on Russian troop withdrawal without consulting parliament. Critics said it left too many former Soviet military personnel in Estonia.
